props.gloss_en: Rav: 'Jerusalem became as a nidda among them' (Lam 1:17) is for a blessing
as a nidda: just as a nidda has permission, so Jerusalem has repair
Rav Yehuda: 'she became as a widow' (Lam 1:1) is for a blessing
as a widow, not an actual widow, but as a woman whose husband went overseas and intends to return to her
Rav Yehuda: 'I too have made you contemptible and base' (Mal 2:9) is for a blessing
for they appoint from us neither river-heads nor geziripatei [officials]
Rav: 'the Lord will smite Israel as the reed is shaken in the water' (1 Kgs 14:15) is for a blessing
R' Yonatan: better the curse with which Achiya the Shilonite cursed Israel than the blessing with which Bilaam the wicked blessed them
R' Yonatan: the verse 'faithful are the wounds of a friend, but the kisses of an enemy are profuse' (Prov 27:6) is what this means

Achiya cursed them with a reed: the reed stands in a place of water, its stock renews, its roots are many; all the winds cannot move it from its place -- it goes and comes with them, and when they subside it stands in its place
but Bilaam the wicked blessed them with a cedar, as it says 'as cedars by the water' (Num 24:6)
the cedar does not stand in a place of water, its stock does not renew, its roots are not many; the winds do not move it, but once the south wind blows on it, it uproots it and turns it on its face
and not only that: the reed merited that a quill be taken from it to write Torah, Prophets and Writings
a person should always be soft as a reed
and not hard as a cedar
the story: R' Elazar b. R' Shimon came from Migdal Gedor, from his teacher's house, riding by the river, very joyful, and his mind was swollen because he had learned much Torah
he did not return the ugly man's greeting, and said: Reika, how ugly that man is! are all your townsmen as ugly as you?
the man: I do not know -- go and say to the Craftsman who made me, 'how ugly is this vessel you made'
knowing he had sinned, he dismounted, prostrated himself and said: I have been humbled before you, forgive me
the man: I do not forgive you until you go to the Craftsman who made me and say, 'how ugly is this vessel you made'
the man to the townsmen: if this is a rabbi, may there not be many like him in Israel -- he did such and such to me
the townsmen: even so, forgive him, for he is a man great in Torah
the man: for your sakes I forgive him, provided he not be accustomed to do so
R' Elazar b. R' Shimon: and therefore [being soft] the reed merited that a quill be taken from it to write a Sefer Torah, tefillin and mezuzot
